38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024).

contribution.value: KVQuant is a sub-4-bit KV cache PTQ method using per-channel pre-RoPE Key quantization, sensitivity-weighted non-uniform datatypes (nuqX), and per-vector dense-and-sparse outlier handling, enabling 10M context length LLaMA-7B inference on an 8-GPU system with under 0.1 perplexity loss.

ev.quote: KVQuant, facilitates low precision KV cache quantization by incorporating several novel methods: (i) Per-Channel Key Quantization, where we adjust the dimension along which we quantize the Key activations to better match the distribution
We used the LLaMA-7B/13B/30B/65B, Llama-2-7B/13B/70B, Llama-3-8B/70B, and Mistral-7B models to evaluate our methodology by measuring perplexity on both Wikitext-2 and C4

Passkey Retrieval Evaluation. We also evaluated the performance of our quantization method on passkey retrieval to assess the model's ability to use its context.

ev.section: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
ev.quote: # KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
Our work, KVQuant, facilitates low precision KV cache quantization
By leveraging per-channel quantization for Keys and per-token quantization for Values, we observe a 3.82 perplexity improvement on Wikitext-2 for 3-bit LLaMA-7B quantization.

we use 16 calibration samples of sequence length 2K from the Wikitext-2 training set (as well as the corresponding gradients) to derive the per-channel scaling factors and zero-points, and to derive the non-uniform datatypes for both Keys and Values.
our nuq2 method provides 8× KV cache compression and enables serving the quantized LLaMA-7B model with a context length of 1M tokens on a single A100 GPU
We report latency benchmarked on an A6000 GPU.
The runtime is reported on a system with an A6000 GPU and an Intel Xeon Gold 6126 CPU.
Runtime for calibration (including k-means) was performed on an Intel Xeon Gold 6442Y CPU
we can achieve 1.2-1.6× and 1.3-1.7× latency savings, respectively, relative to the baseline.

strengths.value: Sub-4-bit KV cache quantization with under 0.1 PPL degradation across LLaMA, Llama-2, Llama-3, Mistral models.

ev.quote: we achieve < 0.1 perplexity degradation with 3-bit quantization on both Wikitext-2 and C4, outperforming existing approaches.

strengths.value: Enables 1M context on single A100 GPU and 10M context on an 8-GPU system for LLaMA-7B.

ev.quote: Our method enables serving LLaMA-7B with a context length of up to 1 million on a single A100-80GB GPU and up to 10 million on an 8-GPU system.

strengths.value: Custom CUDA kernels deliver up to 1.7× speedup vs fp16 matvec on A6000.

ev.quote: We develop custom CUDA kernels for KVQuant, showing that we can achieve up to ~1.7× speedups, compared to baseline fp16 matrix-vector multiplications

strengths.value: Code released at github.com/SqueezeAILab/KVQuant for reproducibility.

ev.quote: Code is available at https://github.com/SqueezeAILab/KVQuant.

weaknesses.value: Latency benchmarks focus on memory-bandwidth-bound generation, not prompt processing where many KV pairs compress at once.

ev.quote: our latency benchmarking results currently focus on memory-bandwidth bound generation rather than prompt processing (where we need to compress multiple Keys and Values at once).

weaknesses.value: Does not address training of long-context models (>100K), only inference.

ev.quote: there is significant work required for training long context length models with greater than 100K context length. This work is orthogonal to our efforts, which are constrained to efficient inference

weaknesses.value: Sparse matrix memory allocation is inefficient; appending new tokens requires copying prior data.

ev.quote: in the current end-to-end implementation, there are inefficiencies in how memory allocation is handled for updating the sparse matrix (where the data corresponding to the previous tokens have to be copied

limitations.value: Only quantizes the KV cache; weights and activations need separate methods (tested with SqueezeLLM weights).
